Should flag

Card blurb wrapping four lines at 1.25

This card description wraps to four lines in a narrow column, and every line sits closer to the next than reading copy at this size can carry.

Accordion answer wrapping three lines at 1.20

The answer paragraph inside this accordion runs to three lines, and at eighteen pixels the lines press together instead of separating.

Footer legal block at 1.17

This footer legal block is the smallest reading copy on the page and still wraps to several lines, so the lines end up nearly touching each other.

Story excerpt bullet at 1.14

  • The excerpt under the lead story runs to two lines of reading copy, and the descenders of the first line reach into the second.

Card description nested inside a heading at 1.10

The service card puts its whole description paragraph inside the card heading, and it still wraps to several lines of reading copy.

Should pass

Display statement set on a paragraph

A statement set at display size carries its own leading, and a ratio under the body floor is exactly what the size wants.

Headline text inside a heading link

The heading puts its text in a child anchor, which is how most cards and most news fronts are marked up.

Card title carrying the heading role

A testimonial card title set as a span with the heading role, wrapping to two lines of title type.

Paragraph set at exactly the floor

This paragraph sets its leading at exactly the floor the rule asks for, so it must never be reported for hitting it.

Mobile variant that is not displayed

The mobile copy of this card blurb is switched off at this width and paints nothing at all for the visitor.

Screen-reader description clipped to a pixel

This description belongs to the video player and is clipped to a single pixel box for assistive technology only.

Analytics payload inside an inline script

Tag manager fallback inside noscript

Single line that never wraps (browser engine only)

This utility class sets tight leading on a label that renders as one single line.
